query: For high-value components operating in aggressive environments, what intervention could improve surface physical and mechanical characteristics? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence that would support it, and an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Annealing an as-deposited amorphous AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) film in air at 800 °C for 1 hour will induce the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide surface layer that improves both the surface mechanical integrity and tribocorrosion (oxidation and wear) resistance of high‐value components compared to untreated films.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-deposited, strongly amorphous AlCrTiZrMo HEA film applied to a high-value component surface
generation.intervention: Anneal the HEA film in air at 800 °C for 1 hour
generation.conditions: The treatment is performed in atmospheric air at 800 °C for 1 hour, and the performance is later evaluated under conditions that simulate aggressive environments (e.g., high temperature combined with corrosive media and mechanical wear testing)
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a dense, stable composite oxide layer (primarily ZrTiO4) on the surface of the HEA film
generation.mechanism: The high-temperature annealing promotes atomic mobility and reaction of the alloy constituents, leading to the development of a protective composite oxide scale that impedes further oxidation, reduces wear, and strengthens the mechanical integrity of the surface
generation.predicted_outcome: The annealed HEA film should exhibit a lower wear rate, a reduced coefficient of friction, and enhanced oxidation resistance compared to the untreated as-deposited film
generation.baseline: Untreated, as-deposited amorphous AlCrTiZrMo HEA film
generation.boundary: The improved performance is expected to hold under conditions typical of aggressive service environments (e.g., high temperatures with corrosive media), and effectiveness is presumed specifically for the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film system
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the improvement in mechanical and tribocorrosion properties remains uncertain and may depend on variations in annealing parameters and details of the aggressive environment

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of high-value component samples coated with the as-deposited amorphous AlCrTiZrMo HEA film. Anneal one group at 800 °C for 1 hour and leave the other group untreated. Subsequently, subject both groups to identical tribocorrosion testing in a simulated aggressive environment (e.g., high-temperature air with corrosive species and mechanical wear using a reciprocating friction setup).
measurements: Surface characterization (e.g., scanning electron microscopy and XPS) to confirm the formation and integrity of the oxide layer
Tribocorrosion metrics, such as wear rate and coefficient of friction
Electrochemical measurements (e.g., changes in open-circuit potential) to assess oxidation resistance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples do not show significantly lower wear rates, reduced coefficients of friction, and improved oxidation resistance—indicating a protective oxide layer—compared to the untreated controls, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion

Filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (FCVAD) has sufficient advantages to obtain multi-component films due to its characteristics of magnetic filtration, high ionization rate (100%) and controllable ion types and ion energy. Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) is obtained by designing a multi-channel for particle transport based on FCVAD, which significantly improves the defects of uncontrollable composition and poor quality in the preparation of HEA films [,]. Thus, in order to improve the performance of mechanical components in extreme service environments, the AlCrTiZrMo film system is determined by selecting elements with a large atomic radius difference and excellent corrosion and high temperature performance. In this work, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film is prepared based on Co-FCVAD. The synergistic interaction between elements at a high temperature in air is discussed, and the changes in microstructure, mechanical properties and tribocorrosion properties of the film after annealing at different temperatures are studied, so as to analyze the protection mechanisms of AlCrTiZrMo HEA films in the simulated scenario of thermal shock.
